answer: I created the project requirements document at requirements.md. Contents capture all provided requirements: backend FastAPI, database PostgreSQL, no Redis, no external paid services, every booking belongs to exactly one student, at most three active bookings per student, and timestamps stored in UTC (timestamptz). I included a constraints summary table and an assumptions/open-questions section distinguishing the spec's verified requirements from assumptions (e.g., the exact definition of an 'active' booking state, student auth/identification, and whether the 3-active limit is enforced at DB vs. application level). I did not implement the API, per the instruction. No tests were run because the task is documentation-only, not code, so there is no executable behavior to verify. Limitations: the 'active' booking lifecycle is not defined in the provided spec, so I documented it as an assumption needing stakeholder confirmation; scope/auth details are likewise flagged as open questions rather than asserted as verified requirements.
